title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Amendment Bill 2005 [2006]

divisions.question: That the amendment ( **Senator Siewert’s** ) be agreed to.

That this bill be now read a second time. That all words after “That” be omitted with a view to substituting the following words: “while not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House: (1) notes that on 20 August 2003, then Leader of the Government in the Senate, Senator Robert Hill, stated in relation to Indigenous heritage protection that the Government recognised the shortcomings in the existing system, that reform was long overdue and that the Government was anxious to have a new and better piece of legislation put in place as quickly as possible; (2) registers its concern that the Howard Government has failed to address the shortcomings in indigenous heritage protection; (3) expresses its concern that the Howard Government has failed to act on the recommendations of the 1996 Evatt Inquiry into the Commonwealth Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act 1984 ; (4) notes that it is now 10 years since the Evatt Inquiry reported, and calls for a comprehensive review of Indigenous heritage protection; and (5) calls on the Government to support the inclusion of a sunset exemption provision in the bill”. That the words proposed to be omitted ( **Mr Albanese’s** amendment) stand part of the question.

speeches.speaker: Jeannie Ferris
speeches.brief: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Amendment Bill 2005 [2006] committee report, along with Hansard records and documents, was presented on behalf of Senator Eggleston for the Environment, Communications, Information Technology and the Arts Legislation Committee.

speeches.speaker: Kim Carr
speeches.brief: Labor supported the bill but called it grossly inadequate, criticizing the Howard government for failing to consult Indigenous communities, neglecting the 1996 Evatt report recommendations, and politicising heritage listings such as Wave Hill and the Aboriginal tent embassy.

speeches.speaker: Eric Abetz
speeches.brief: The bill's amendments allow overseas institutions to exhibit Indigenous cultural heritage in Australia and repeal Victoria-specific provisions to enable new Victorian legislation; the speaker opposed Senator Siewert's proposed amendments as unnecessary.

speeches.speaker: Bob Brown
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Burrup Peninsula in Western Australia, home to up to one million ancient rock art depictions, is being destroyed by industrial development, with 40% of the site already lost, and called on the federal government to protect it as World Heritage, criticising the Western Australian government and Woodside for allowing the destruction. He also supported a bill to issue certificates for overseas Indigenous artworks brought to Australia for exhibition.

speeches.speaker: Rod Kemp
speeches.brief: The bill is criticised as a missed opportunity that only partially implements the 1996 Evatt report recommendations, with the government accused of delaying reform for a decade. Two positive elements are noted: strengthening legal protections for international borrowings of Indigenous artefacts and returning heritage administration to Victoria, but the Greens also condemn the government’s secret internal review process.

speeches.speaker: Rachel Siewert
speeches.brief: The government is conducting an internal review of the act without public submissions, timelines, or transparency, which the speaker called a missed opportunity for a proper, thorough review.

acts.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Amendment Act 2006
